doc.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 2, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Why she cancelled: family first, and fellow musicians' stress
summary: She explains she put family first, urged her parents to get out of Europe, and travelled with Paolo Alderighi and Stephanie Trick.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You anticipated a question I was going to ask and that is most musicians were sitting waiting for the phone to ring and the more it rang, the more we knew what was coming. Like okay this is cancelled, now who’s next? But I was going to ask if you had to initiate cancellations and indeed you have quite a —

Yes because as you know, family comes first. So not only I couldn’t get back to Australia — because I’d been on the road and that’s the worst situation for a virus like this. So I knew I couldn’t go back to Australia right away, then I wouldn’t know how I would come back to Connecticut to be with my husband and stepson. So I had my parents on FaceTiming and said, “You’ve got to get out of Europe, you’ve got to get out now. And I said well I have to go home, I mean I have to come here. And fortunately I was able to get that flight. It was very stressful because I was also with two other American musicians, Paolo Alderighi and Stephanie Trick. We were doing some gigs together at the beginning of March. And they were also very stressed because Paolo’s parents were in Milan but they couldn’t get back to Milan because Italy was in a very bad way at that stage. And Germany was looking bad. And of course it hadn’t really hit the U.S. quite as bad, it wasn’t quite here yet, or it was quite here yet but we didn’t really know about it. And that whole time was very stressful. But I’m glad I did the right thing and actually one of the promoters called the next day and cancelled and apologized for being so mad. And I was glad in a way you know?
